response.query: What precise mathematical definition of per-batch spectral summary S_{t,d}(f) (averaging rule, log-scaling, normalization) yields reproducible, low-variance estimates for feature vectors of length N?
response.answer: Per-batch spectral summary S_{t,d}(f) normalizes feature vectors by averaging, log-scaling, and normalizing to ensure reproducibility and low variance. It uses minibatch statistics for normalization.

results.title: Batch Normalization Explained - Lei Mao's Log Book
results.content: In this blog post, I am going to review batch normalization again on its mathematical definition and intuitions. Given inputs $x$ over a minibatch of size $m$, $B = \{x\_1, x\_2, …, x\_m\}$, by applying transformation of your inputs using some learned parameters $\gamma$ and $\beta$, the outputs could be expressed as $B’ = \{y\_1, y\_2, …, y\_m\}$, where $y\_i = {\text{BN}}\_{\gamma, \beta} (x\_i)$. More concretely, we first calculate the mean and the variance of the samples from the minibatch. \mu\_B = \frac{1}{m} \sum\_{i=1}^{m} x\_i \\. \sigma\_B^2 = \frac{1}{m} \sum\_{i=1}^{m} (x\_i - \mu\_B)^2 \\. \hat{x}\_{i} = \frac{x\_i-\mu\_B}{\sqrt{\sigma\_B^2 + \epsilon}}. During the test phase, specifically when you only have one test sample, doing batch normalization as the one in the training phase does not make sense, because your outputs at each layer of the network will be exactly zero. When momentum = 1.0, the running means and variances are always the means and variance of the first minibatch, which could also be highly biased.

results.title: [PDF] Spectral Batch Normalization: Normalization in the Frequency Domain
results.content: In this paper, we introduce spectral batch normalization (SBN), a novel effective method to improve generalization by normalizing feature maps in the frequency (spectral) domain. The activations of residual networks without batch normalization (BN) tend to explode exponentially in the depth of the network at initialization. However, we show experimentally that, despite the approximate additive penalty of BN, feature maps in deep neural networks (DNNs) tend to explode at the beginning of the network and that feature maps of DNNs contain large values during the whole training. In our experiments, we empirically show that SBN prevents exploding feature maps at initialization and large feature map values during the training. Moreover, the normalization of feature maps in the frequency domain leads to more uniform distributed frequency components. We show experimentally that using SBN in addition to standard regularization methods improves the performance of DNNs by a relevant margin, e.g. ResNet50 on CIFAR-100 by 2.31%, on ImageNet by 0.71% (from 76.80% to 77.51%) and VGG19 on CIFAR-100 by 0.66%.

results.title: Batch Normalization
results.content: This is a PyTorch implementation of Batch Normalization from paper Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift. The paper defines *Internal Covariate Shift* as the change in the distribution of network activations due to the change in network parameters during training. During the beginning of the training l1​ outputs (inputs to l2​) could be in distribution N(0.5,1). (ignoring variance), let x^=x−E[x] where x=u+b and b is a trained bias and E[x] is an outside gradient computation (pre-computed constant). First simplification is that it normalizes each feature independently to have zero mean and unit variance: x^(k)=Var[x(k)]​x(k)−E[x(k)]​ where x=(x(1)...x(d)) is the d-dimensional input. The second simplification is to use estimates of mean E[x(k)] and variance Var[x(k)] from the mini-batch for normalization; instead of calculating the mean and variance across the whole dataset. y(k)=γ(k)x^(k)+β(k) where y(k) is the output of the batch normalization layer. We need to know E[x(k)] and Var[x(k)] in order to perform the normalization.
